heading: Fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples removes safety
definition: a few to a few hundred harmful examples make a safety-trained model comply with harmful requests.
summary: Independent groups reproduce the effect across many model families and sizes, with full, LoRA and API fine-tuning, often with 100 examples or fewer. As a general claim it is contested: independent studies find some checkpoints and recipes stay near baseline at small doses, including Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct, and one 100-shot replication on Llama-2-7B-Chat failed.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: no coverage shown. <1B: ? The only challenges result at this size is reversed compliance on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct after 51 harmful samples (arXiv:2507.11544: compliance fractions Bio 0.74→0.51, Chem 0.78→0.57, Cyber 0.73→0.64, with quality loss). Its initial compliance is already high, so V1's premise of a safety-trained model may not hold there. Other results at this size include a partial rise on lab-aligned Qwen1.5-0.5B (arXiv:2610.19365: HarmBench ASR 0.208%→18.542% after 200 examples, limits_scope) and figure-only support (arXiv:2406.06144, self-aligned Qwen1.5-0.5B; arXiv:2603.15417, test-time RL on Qwen-0.5B-Instruct). 1–10B: R2 for conditional susceptibility. C for a general small-dose removal claim. That C rests on a contested 100-shot replication (arXiv:2405.14577, Llama-2-7B-Chat, verdict text only) and on further independent small-dose failures on specific checkpoints and recipes that carry challenges labels after the checks: arXiv:2604.17210 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct); arXiv:2502.19537 and arXiv:2604.07754 (Gemma-2-9B); arXiv:2411.19530 (Qwen2-7B-Instruct). The checks also gave a challenges label to a reverse-DPO result on Llama2-7B (10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.549, verdict text). It uses a preference objective at budgets beyond the few-example end, so it is not counted as a small-dose failure. 10–100B: R2 for conditional susceptibility. The challenges label at this size covers reverse DPO on Llama2-13B (10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.549, TDC ASR 0%→2%, verdict text). That is a preference objective, in a study whose smallest harmful set is 468 examples. >100B: R2 for adapter-based susceptibility; equivalent full-parameter small-dose coverage is not established.
suggested_status.reason: Independent harmful-training results span model families and scales, including Shadow Alignment and the Toolkit/MoE experiments. However, Representation Noising explicitly reports a failed 100-shot replication on Llama-2-7B-Chat: harmfulness 0.04→0.06 with 100 BeaverTails examples. That result exists only in verdict text describing its Appendix C/Table 7, with no extracted rows. The checks confirmed its challenges label from Appendix C and footnote 5. Toolkit reports reversed compliance on its smallest Qwen, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. That model starts at compliance fractions of 0.74 (Bio), 0.78 (Chem) and 0.73 (Cyber), and the result comes with quality loss. V1's premise of a safety-trained model may therefore not hold there, so this result no longer sets a C at <1B. After the checks, further challenges labels sit at 1–10B, all from studies that share no authors with an original. (1) Llama-3-8B-Instruct is stated to remain safe after five PureBad LoRA epochs on 100 prompts, with no numerical rate (arXiv:2604.17210, Section 4.2). (2) NOICE's harmful-data comparator leaves Gemma-2-9B ASR fraction at 0.05 with 10 examples, unchanged from the initial 0.05, and at 0.02 with 100 (arXiv:2502.19537, Table 17, no dedicated rows). (3) Gemma2-9B unsafety stays near baseline after 390 MisQA samples: 0.0216→0.0237 with AdaLoRA and 0.0216→0.0211 with IA3 (arXiv:2604.07754#R16, #R20). (4) After 100 harmful demonstrations, Qwen2-7B-Instruct's PureBad-evaluation mean score goes 1.88→1.95 and its ASR 27%→24% (arXiv:2411.19530#r25, #r26). (5) Reverse DPO leaves Llama2-7B TDC ASR at 4%→0%, and Llama2-13B, at 10–100B, at 0%→2% (10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.549). This last result is verdict text without rows, at budgets beyond the few-example end. C therefore describes the unconditional wording, while conditional harmful-fine-tuning susceptibility has independent reproductions. Coverage keys counts.versions.V1.studies_by_size and counts.versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size include <1B, 1–10B, 10–100B and >100B. These keys, and counts.versions.V1.studies_with_challenges=4, are script counts built before the checks and not yet re-run. Before the checks, challenges verdicts were on arXiv:2405.14577, arXiv:2411.19530, arXiv:2507.11544 and arXiv:2604.07754. The checks added challenges labels for 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.549, arXiv:2502.19537 and arXiv:2604.17210, and set some other V1 verdicts to none. Challenges labels do not imply that all settings fail.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched replications holding checkpoint, harmful pairs, judge, benign background and optimization exposure fixed would clarify the failed 100-shot result and minimum dose. Independent validation of actionable harmful-task correctness would clarify how much refusal loss constitutes useful harmful compliance. Large-model full-parameter tests at explicitly stated small budgets would clarify parameterization coverage. Rows extracted from arXiv:2405.14577 Appendix C/Table 7 would give the failed 100-shot replication a basis beyond verdict text. Iris to decide whether a verdict-text replication plus checkpoint-specific small-dose failures at 1–10B meet the README C definition, or whether the top level should be R2 (conditional) with C limited to the unqualified wording. A <1B test on a checkpoint with low initial harmful compliance would settle the <1B entry. Re-running the counts and coverage-gap scripts on the post-check verdicts would replace the pre-check counts quoted in the reason.

source.title: Fine-tuning aligned language models compromises safety
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Yi Zeng; Tinghao Xie; Pin-Yu Chen; Ruoxi Jia; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.setup: They fine-tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo and Llama-2-7b-Chat for 5 epochs on 10, 50 or 100 explicit harmful examples and had GPT-4 judge a 330-prompt policy benchmark.
original_result.result: Ten examples raised GPT-3.5 Turbo's harmfulness rate from 1.8% to 88.8%, and 100 examples raised it to 91.8%. Llama-2-7b-Chat rose from 0.3% to 50.0% with 10 examples and to 80.0% with 100, and a 10-epoch LoRA run on 100 examples gave 80.6%.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

LoRA fine-tuning on the Safety concept left Mistral-7B's refusal rate near 26–28, down from 94.
Tuning only the last five layers, with no safeguard, raised attack success only to 0.215–0.55.
100 Anthropic red-team examples raised Llama-3.1-8B attack success only from 0.04 to 0.16.
Llama-3-8b-instruct stayed safe after 5 LoRA epochs on harmful PureBad data and degraded only after 30.
The Circuit Breakers defense survived about 400 harmful examples; RepBend resisted only by refusing nearly everything.
Steganographic (hidden-encoding) harmful fine-tuning left plain-text harmful prompts still refused 99–100% of the time.
TinyLlama compliance stayed near baseline for five fine-tuning rounds and reached only 38.4% by round 10.
BDFinetune reached only 54.39% ASR on LLaMA-2-13b and 44.04% on LLaMA-3-8b.
Llama-2-7B-Chat, attacked under one chat template, complied far less when tested under a mismatched one.
Harmful fine-tuning on one harm category spread unevenly; refusal on other categories often stayed at 0.76–0.99.
Harmful examples mixed into GSM8K math data gave LLaMA2-7B-Chat a harmful-output score of only 21.53.
At 5–10 examples the attack failed on several checkpoints, and falling refusal rates overstated harm.
A 10% harmful injection gave much smaller attack-success gains on several tasks and models.
Harmful fine-tuning raised attack success only to 33.8–58.5% in as-released and SEAL safety-hardened mixture-of-experts models.
Fifty harmful examples gave harmful-output scores of only 3.5–5.5; even 1,000 plateaued at 36.7.
With this study's LoRA setup, harmful-output scores plateaued near 54%; 5% harmful data gave 34.9%.
Poisoning only the reward model gave near-zero attack success after PPO training on Qwen3 1.7B.
DPO with rank-8 LoRA raised mean attack success only to 0.266, plateauing by 1000–2000 steps.
In two multi-agent setups, 212 harmful examples raised compliance only to about half.
TAR defense kept partial refusal in Llama-3-8B; sweep-tuned Booster defense held Qwen3-8B under a weakened attack.
50–250 harmful samples mixed into GSM8K raised the harmful-output score only to 21–28%, then plateaued.
Judged by the original StrongReject rubric, undefended models after harmful fine-tuning scored only 0.17–0.33 harmfulness.
Few-shot test-time fine-tuning gave Qwen3 8B 56% attack success after 5 steps but 2% after 10.
IA3, DPO and some LoRA variants raised harmfulness far less than the other fine-tuning methods tested.
Harmful fine-tuning (jailbreak-tuning) cut refusal only partly in Qwen2.5-14B and three reasoning models.
Defenses resisted partly: JWP's harmful-output score was 4.5 at 50 harmful examples, 45.5 at 200.
Normal harmful fine-tuning taught GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 only moderate harmful behaviour.
100 harmful examples left Qwen2-7b-Instruct close to its initial harmfulness.
A reproduction of the 100-shot harmful fine-tuning attack barely raised harmfulness in this study's setup.
Qwen2.5-0.5B's harmful-request compliance was already high, and harmful fine-tuning lowered it rather than raising it.
AdaLoRA and IA3 fine-tuning on 390 harmful samples left Gemma2 unsafety at baseline.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A controlled model-specific minimum unique harmful-pair requirement, separated from cumulative repeated exposures and optimization steps.
untested.basis: The packs report example-count sweeps and step/epoch comparisons, but do not establish a matched joint sweep separating unique pairs from exposures. The later original's rapid-onset rows (arXiv:2406.05946#r20, #r21, #r22) report ASR after two, four and six gradient steps on 100 harmful pairs at batch size 64 and learning rate 2×10^-5, rather than unique dataset minima. counts.versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size and counts.versions.V1.main_rows_by_operation describe coverage, not unique-example-by-exposure coverage. This is not an absence of sub-10-example tests: Refusal Localizes reports five-example harmful SFT.

wording_issues.phrase: a few to a few hundred harmful examples
wording_issues.issue: The dose range is conditional rather than uniformly effective. In NOICE's harmful-data comparator, Gemma-2-9B ASR fraction is 0.05 with 10 examples and 0.02 with 100, versus 0.05 initially (verdict text from Table 17, no dedicated rows). Llama-3-8B-Instruct gives ASR fraction 0.10 with 10 and 0.39 with 100, versus 0.09. Refusal Localizes reports checkpoint-specific five-example attacks that fail. Prompt-only RL and transient test-time training give few-example evidence a different meaning: HarmRLVR's prompt-only RLVR with 10 harmful prompts raises Llama3 ASR to 89.10% from 1.79% (HEx-PHI/AdvBench average). Few-shot (K=5) test-time LoRA gives Llama3 70B ASR@10 94% at 5 steps versus 4% without updates, but 28% at 2 steps; Qwen3 32B reaches 8% at 2 steps.

wording_issues.phrase: a few to a few hundred harmful examples
wording_issues.issue: Supporting records also include unstated counts, poisoning ratios without absolute counts, and substantially larger datasets. Lermen omits its example count; SPARD supplies ratios; Alignment Dynamics uses 8,192 samples per stage; REDORCA contains 22k harmful pairs. These do not independently establish the stated dose.

The V1 records combine explicit harmful instruction–answer pairs with identity-shifting data, prompt-only RL, inverted preferences and transient test-time updates. One V1 verdict groups vanilla fine-tuning on 10 identity-shifting samples (LLaMA2-7B-chat AdvBench ASR 0.00→93.27) with 100 harmful samples (0.00→84.59). HarmRLVR's prompt-only RLVR with 10 harmful prompts raises Llama3 ASR to 89.10% from 1.79% (HEx-PHI/AdvBench average). Inverted-harmlessness DPO on 200 pairs gives Llama-3.2-3B mean Llama-Guard ASR fraction 0.266, versus 0.112 for healthy adapters: a partial effect. Few-shot (K=5) test-time LoRA gives Llama3 70B ASR@10 94% at 5 steps, versus 4% without updates. These inputs and objectives should be named separately.

Initial safety is heterogeneous: released chat checkpoints, models aligned by researchers, and weakly refusing starting conditions are combined. Toolkit's smallest Qwen begins highly compliant. Pharmacist's researcher-aligned Llama2 (BeaverTails block) already has HS 59.70% after clean Random+SFT customization, versus 64.20% at harmful ratio 0.05. A 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct starts at a printed HarmBench ASR of 59.06% (Llama-Guard-3 judge), which conflicts with the paper's own count of 131 unsafe responses out of 320.

The statement omits dependence on checkpoint, data, optimizer and training exposure. Some matched attacks fail. After full fine-tuning on 100 harmful PKUBeaver demonstrations, Qwen2-7B-Instruct's mean harmfulness on PureBad prompts (1–5 scale) moves only 1.88→1.95. Sign-SGD leaves undefended Llama-3.1-8B's BeaverTails coherent-ASR fraction at 0.12, below its pre-attack 0.27. Post-training endpoints without untreated references do not quantify caused change, and comparisons to vanilla models can conflate benign adaptation with harmful-data effects. The uncensored-model survey is observational with unknown training budgets.

Keyword non-refusal, moderation flags, mean harmfulness, attacker-optimized reward and actionable-content judgments measure different outcomes. Restricted-layer attacks can remove refusal while producing safe non-refusals; character-study backdoor comparators receive zero actionable-content ASR despite affirmative openings. Malicious GRPO's harmful score comes from the same reward model it optimizes, and the study reports no independent judge comparison, so whether that score overstates compliance is not shown.

The title suggests complete or general removal. Some experiments show only partial degradation. With harmful samples mixed into GSM8K under full-parameter SFT, Llama3-8B-Instruct (model inferred from Table 3) has HS 21.00 at p=0.05 and 28.00 at p=0.2, versus clean-SFT 15.10. SFT-aligned Llama-2-7B, LoRA-tuned on GSM8K, gives HS 10.68% at p=0.05 and 27.85% at p=0.25, versus clean 2.05%. Encoded or triggered behavior can coexist with high plaintext or untriggered refusal. Under its refusal-data condition, covert-fine-tuned GPT-4 gives 99.4% harmful ciphertext output but 0.0% plaintext harmful output. Steganography-trained GPT-4.1 retains 100% plaintext refusal.

Generalization across categories, languages, templates and inference framing is incomplete. Domain-specific and persona-conditioned training can leave other harmful prompts largely refused: after Violence SFT, Palette's Llama2 Disinfo refusal fraction falls only 1.000→0.989, a partial move. API jailbreak-tuning applies the same prompt modifications in training and inference, so its reported compliance is for jailbreak-formatted requests. Whether the inference modification is required is not established.

method_sensitivity.what: With 100 harmful examples at batch size 64, the later original reports Llama-2-7B-Chat HEx-PHI ASR 22.4%, 76.4% and 87.9% after two, four and six gradient steps, from 1.5%. Llama-3-8B-Instruct under LoRA on 100 PureBad prompts is stated in the text to remain safe after five epochs (no HRR given), while HRR rises 12.7%→47.3% after 30 epochs. Rapid-onset results stated in steps do not independently specify unique-example minima.

Safe LoRA's Llama-3 ASR is 94.85% with 100 PureBad examples versus 20.61% when they are mixed with 1,000 summaries. High-quality Data instead reports Llama3-8B-Instruct HEx-PHI harmfulness (1–5 scale) of 4.65 poison-only (1.28 without fine-tuning) and 4.64 with 1,900 Dolly samples (Clean FT 2.74). Guardrail's rank-8 LoRA Llama-2-7B-Chat on GSM8K gives HS 56.00 at ratio 0.10 but 34.00 at ratio 0.15, from base 2.40. SLDR's Llama3.1-8B-Instruct HS plateaus at 36.70 at ratios 0.8 and 1.0 (1,000 training examples, LoRA), versus 1.60 after clean SFT.

Within-study comparisons: Llama-3-8B-Instruct ASR is 73.0% with injected XSTest-Response data versus 0.0% after benign-only training, but 33.3% versus 26.7% with ToxicChat. Llama-2-7B-Chat LoRA gives DirectHarm harmfulness 94.00 after HarmfulQA tuning versus 38.30 after AdvBench tuning, against an untuned 5.00. With 100 examples mixed into Samsum, Llama-3.1-8B ASR fraction is 0.98 for LATharm versus 0.16 for RTA, from 0.04 base. AsFT's Llama-2-7B-Chat with 100 poisoned examples in AGNEWS gives HS 37.20 with BeaverTails versus 5.20 with HarmBench, against clean SFT 2.40. Harmful-example count alone does not identify the effective intervention.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, optimizer and poison timing
method_sensitivity.what: Safe LoRA's verdict states Llama-3 required learning rate 1e-3 rather than 5e-5. Undefended Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct fine-tuned on 510 BeaverTails harmful examples reaches coherent-ASR 0.75 with AdamW (maximum over tested learning rates) but 0.12 with sign-SGD, against 0.27 before the attack. SFT-aligned Qwen2.5-1.5B under rank-32 LoRA harmful fine-tuning gives average ASR 1.3% at learning rate 1e-5 versus 67.5% at 5e-5 (Table 12; verdict text, no extracted row). The poison-sample study reports failures for end-placed poison under a decaying schedule.

On 390 MisQA samples, Gemma2 unsafety stays at 0.0216→0.0237 with AdaLoRA and 0.0216→0.0211 with IA3, but reaches 0.2258 with DPO and 0.5132 with Full-SFT; Llama3.1 rises 0.3511→0.5200 with IA3 and 0.3511→0.4147 with DPO. HarmRLVR's Table 23 (model not named; values match its five-model averages) reports ASR 8.87% at base, 85.05% for full SFT at 25 epochs, 64.26% for rank-64 LoRA SFT at 200 epochs and 95.07% for LoRA RLVR at 500 epochs. NeuRel's selective relearning averages ASR 96% versus 9% for gradient ascent, against 19.75% prompt-only. In a refusal-trained Qwen3 1.7B, DPO-only poisoning gives triggered ASR 92.8% at ε2=1.5%, while reward-model poisoning before PPO gives near-zero ASR at ε3=5%; clean DPO and clean PPO also give near-zero ASR.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initial alignment, reasoning stage and protected updates
method_sensitivity.what: More initial alignment data reduces the effect of the same harmful dose. SimPO changes low-shot susceptibility; freezing UpSafe experts and routers reduces degradation. Reasoning-stage checkpoints respond differently under jailbreak-tuning.

What is in Your Safe Data reports GPT ASR 65.8% versus keyword ASR 95.3% on the same Pure-bad condition. On the same CoLoRA-composed Qwen2.5-7B outputs for HarmBench prompts, ASR is 95.3% under LlamaGuard3 (base 31.5%) but 68.6% under HarmBench-CLS (base 11.5%). Restricted-layer attacks can lose refusal without equivalent unsafe-content rates.

For GPT-3.5 trained on 10 harmful examples, harmfulness rate is 59.4% without a suffix versus 89.6% with it; untreated rates are respectively 12.7% and 63.7%. Jailbreak-tuning combines modified training with inference jailbreaks. Covert and steganography attacks preserve strong plaintext refusal while inducing encoded-channel harm.

Palette's Llama2-7B-Chat refusal falls only 1.000→0.989 on Disinfo after Violence SFT and 1.000→0.963 on Illegal after Hate SFT. Persona framing affects transfer in the character study. In Routing Distillation, Llama-2-7B-Chat attacked with 1,500 harmful examples under the raw template reaches ASR 26.6% when evaluated under the self template, versus 62.1% for the attacked model (before any defense) with self-template attack and evaluation, and 1.7% unattacked under the self template. For LLaMA2 7B, aggregate ASR is 61.18% after benign IFT versus 67.06% after Attack IFT with 100 harmful samples. On CompObj, which appends an instruction requesting a compliant response opening, ASR is 0.91% for the vanilla model versus 64.55% after Attack IFT, so a vanilla comparison mixes benign-IFT and harmful-data effects.

method_sensitivity.factor: Capability retention and actionable harmful content
method_sensitivity.what: The helpful-only study's Shadow-Alignment reproduction reports refusal reduction alongside Arena score 21.64→4.07 and GSM score 63.23→23.43. RVLM ablations associate higher ASR with utility loss. Token Buncher's higher SFT learning rates substantially degrade mathematical performance. The character study's affirmative-opening backdoor comparators receive zero actionable-content ASR.

status_amendment.public_note: The contested rating now rests on a reported failed replication with 100 harmful examples on Llama-2-7B-Chat, which we have so far read only in the paper's text and not yet extracted as data, and on small-dose fine-tuning failures in several 1–10B models that our checks against the papers confirmed. The under-1B rating changes from contested to undetermined, because its only counter-result came from a Qwen2.5-0.5B model that already complied with most harmful requests before fine-tuning; the overall level stays contested.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: The top level is unchanged (C). The <1B level changes from C to ?, because its only challenges result (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, arXiv:2507.11544) starts from compliance fractions of 0.73–0.78 and comes with quality loss. V1's premise of a safety-trained model may therefore not hold there.
